args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service started failing health checks (unhealthy, error rate 18%) in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Checked after the rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to redeploy it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open.

- **Rollback:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was unhealthy with an 18% error rate in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production, so I rolled back to it in all three regions. Checking afterwards, every region is on v2.3.0, the service is passing health checks and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-up needed: find the root cause before anyone redeploys v2.3.1.

The test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging before it went to production, so it's worth finding out why that didn't stop the deploy. I noted this in the incident.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
